subject: Q3 transient headroom request: short-lived GPU buffer for regression sweep
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Park <susan@helixhealth.ai>, CloudZone Ops <partner-ops@cloudzone.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 transient headroom request: short-lived GPU buffer for regression sweep

Team —

Quick ask from Product/Integrations. Helix Health is running a full regression sweep across three large models next week (models are open variants we host for them). The sweep is time-sensitive — their compliance window requires all tests completed before their board meeting on Aug 2. They expect bursty traffic that will temporarily push the EU-dedicated pool close to capacity.

What we need: a short-lived transient headroom allocation in the EU-dedicated pool to cover an estimated 120 GPU-hours over a 72-hour window (Jul 30–Aug 1). This is not a long-term carve; it's a temporary buffer to avoid preemption and keep latency SLOs for production tenants.

Key constraints:
- Autoscale policy currently enforces conservative caps for the EU pool during business hours; without an exception the sweep will be throttled.
- Helix will reimburse overage under an agreed PO (they've uploaded a provisional commitment).
- We need monitoring hooks + an automatic deprovision at window end.

Requested ops asks:
1) Temporary autoscale exemption (increase max concurrent slots by ~20% for Jul 30 00:00 UTC through Aug 1 23:59 UTC).
2) A named tag and cost-center for chargeback so Finance can reconcile the PO.
3) Ops runbook for quick rollback if noisy neighbor signals spike (I attached a preliminary schedule and cost estimate).

Can you confirm feasibility and who on infra needs to sign off? If we can get a conditional sign-off by Friday (Jul 28), Helix will lock the dates and we can finalize the PO.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: regression-schedule.csv, cost-estimate.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 transient headroom request: short-lived GPU buffer for regression sweep

Olga —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Two quick clarifications before Ops can start drafting the waiver:
1) Is this strictly EU region (we need the region to scope capacity and to check any region-specific reservations).
2) Will Helix accept spot-equivalent preemptible instances for non-latency-critical parts of the sweep, or do they require sustained low-latency on pinned GPUs? If the former, we can reduce required headroom.

Process note: per the reserved-capacity & exception policy link below, temporary autoscale waivers require a product owner sign-off + cost-center tagging + explicit deprovision time. I'll loop in Infra once those are confirmed.

I've added a pointer to the policy: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/policies/dedicated-capacity-exceptions

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudZone Ops <partner-ops@cloudzone.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 transient headroom request: short-lived GPU buffer for regression sweep

Kim / Olga —

Operational constraints and suggested mitigation from Infra side:

1) Region: EU (confirmed) — we have two candidate pools (eu-west-1a: lower utilization but slower NVLink; eu-central: higher throughput).
2) Autoscale waiver: we can scratch a temporary increase, but we'd prefer to limit to 80 GPU-hours unless Finance confirms PO terms. Larger increases require a temporary reservation carve and pre-notice to other enterprise tenants.
3) Suggested approach to minimize risk:
   - Allocate a named burst lane: tag = helix_regression_2028_q3; cost_center = HELIX-PO-7782.
   - Limit per-tenant concurrency to avoid noisy neighbor.
   - Enforce a hard deprovision at 2028-08-01T23:59:00Z via automation (no manual overrides).
   - Add a circuit-breaker metric (apdex > 0.85 on prod traffic) to auto-throttle the sweep.

I've attached a lightweight ops runbook (ops-runbook.md) with the automation snippet for deprovision and JIRA playbook (INFRA-4921). If product can confirm the 80 GPU-hour option and Helix signs PO, Infra will submit the waiver and pre-stage images in eu-west-1a.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: ops-runbook.md

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 16:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 transient headroom request: short-lived GPU buffer for regression sweep

Marcus / Kim / Olga —

Conditional approval granted. Approvals and constraints below: 

- Approved headroom: 80 GPU-hours (eu-west-1a) for the window 2028-07-30T00:00Z through 2028-08-01T23:59Z.
- Conditions:
  * Tag must be applied exactly as proposed (helix_regression_2028_q3) for automatic cost attribution.
  * Finance needs the finalized PO number before we flip the waiver (OLGA, please confirm PO# by 2028-07-29 17:00 PDT).
  * Automation must enforce hard deprovision (no manual override without VP approval).
  * Infra to enable the circuit-breaker/apdex threshold and notify #infra-ops channel on Slack if triggered.

Olga — please confirm you will: (1) get PO# from Helix; (2) update the Drive folder with the signed PO and lightweight SOW; (3) confirm whether Helix will accept any preemptible capacity for non-critical tests (this could unlock more capacity). Once PO# and the SOW are in Drive I will sign the waiver in the exceptions tracker (INFRA-4921).

Thanks — quick and tight execution here will keep this contained and low impact for other customers.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Capacity & Infra Operations
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
